coverage.finding: The native tile shows the folio number in the top-left corner at about native [365,335,150,140]. It reads '259' with a superscript 'b' above and after the 9, followed by a dot. r001 '259b.' matches the source. The 'b' reading is likely but not certain.

There is a small isolated pencil '?' at about native [2960,3115,45,80]. In tile 1604/1608 it sits at local x≈1370, y≈1520. The same mark appears in the left-edge strip of the fol. 260 overview, at about y≈915/1500. This confirms it is on fol. 259b and is not a separate fol. 260 mark. No text is written next to it on this page.

There is a pencil mark at about native [2685,4165,105,155]. It is a small '?' followed by a long slanted stroke. A short branch at the foot of the stroke gives it a 'λ'-like or tick-like shape. The literal reading '?/' is acceptable only as an approximation, so the uncertainty should mention the λ-like form.
This is the inventory's first unattached mark, which had no ID. It is the same as candidate added block b901.
This is the inventory's second unattached mark, which had no ID. It is the same as candidate added block b902.

The strip beyond the gutter at x≳3200 shows fragments 'cl', 'd' and 'a' at y≈650, 760 and 880, and a tick at y≈1530. Their heights match the fol. 260 shelfmarks 'd. 716 (1)', 'd. 726 (5)' and 'd. 737', and the tick matches '√c. 91 (2)'. They are fragments of the facing page, not target records. This disposition is correct.

review.boundary_review: The principal page runs from about x 312 to the gutter at about x 3200. The left-edge '?' in the fol. 260 overview is this page's b901, so it should not be counted twice. The dark notch at the top edge near x 780–840 is physical damage.
